cards.title: Introduction to React Forms
cards.content:
Handling forms is a crucial part of building interactive React applications. Unlike traditional HTML forms where the DOM handles form data, React prefers using Controlled Components, where state is the single source of truth.

const [value, setValue] = useState('');

options.text: Form data is handled by the DOM itself.
React state handles the form data and input values.
Inputs cannot be validated before submission.

cards.title: Uncontrolled Components & Refs
cards.content:
Sometimes you need Uncontrolled Components where form values are grabbed directly from the DOM using the useRef hook instead of writing an event handler for every keystroke.

const inputRef = useRef(null);
// access via inputRef.current.value

content.text: To create an uncontrolled component and reference a DOM element directly in React, we use the _____ hook.

cards.title: Advanced Forms with Libraries
cards.content: As forms grow, managing state manually leads to performance bottlenecks and boilerplate. Libraries like React Hook Form or Formik optimize re-renders and simplify validation schema integration with tools like Yup or Zod.

pairs.right: DOM drives the input value via Ref

items.text: User types into the input field.
onChange event fires, triggering state update.
React re-renders the component with the new state.
User clicks submit, triggering onSubmit handler.

cards.title: Summary & Best Practices
cards.content:
Always remember to:

  • Use controlled components for dynamic validation and dependency.
  • Prevent default form submission behavior using e.preventDefault().
  • Consider libraries for complex, multi-step enterprise forms.
